newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Appetite still strong for techs.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Appetite still strong for techs.

text.p: Investors' appetite for options -- mainly call options -- on technology stocks remained strong Wedensday even as the stocks extended their rallies, traders said.
"We've had a lot of people just fueling the fire buying into it," one options trader said, citing heavy interest in Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp options in particular.
"We haven't had too many people taking anything off the table," he said. "We've had net buyers."
By 1450 CDT/1950 GMT, the technology-laden Nasdaq composite index .IXIC was up 39.34 points, or 2.6 percent, at a record 1,581.45.
The Nasdaq 100 index .NDX was up even more, gaining 46.24, or 4.4 percent, to 1,105.25.
"It's just incredible. They just keep coming after the techs," said Jesse Stamer, a general partner at TradeNet LP, a designated primary market maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.

"It seems to me the big companies like the Intels continue to surprise on the upside," he said. "I don't see it slowing down until we're through the earnings cycle, and that's probably a couple weeks away."
On Tuesday, heavy trading in Intel options led to record single day volume in equity options at the American Stock Exchange.
The exchange said 623,980 equity options traded Tuesday, beating the prior record of 580,330 contracts set December 11, 1996.
Intel, which after the close of trading yesterday reported better than expected second quarter earnings of $0.92 a share, led the pack in options trading Wednesday as well.
Most of the action was on the call side. The Intel July 85 call traded 15,985 contracts, the July 80 call traded 15,775 and the the August 90 call traded 14,465.
On the put side, the July 80, July 85, August 80 and January 65 were also active, with turnover of 9,350, 6,190, 4,940 and 2,940 contracts, respectively.
Intel shares were up 7-15/64 at 88-3/8. Volume was a heavy 46.7 million shares.

"I think people are scrambling to cover all their shorts," Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said of the Intel options activity. "It's the same thing that's been driving the market all along."
On the Pacific Exchange, options on Microsoft remained active ahead of quarterly earnings scheduled for release Thursday.
Elsewhere in the group, International Business Machines Corp options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange and 3Com Corp options on the Pacific Exchange were busy.
